ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rhombus ABCD, with A on the left side, C on the right side, D above, and B below; A and C are opposite vertices, and B and D are opposite vertices, therefore AC and BD are the two diagonals of the rhombus. Reasoning: The perimeter of the rhombus is 52 meters, so each side length is 52/4 = 13 meters. It is known that diagonal AC = 24 meters, so half of AC is 12 meters. The two diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other perpendicularly, therefore half of AC, half of BD, and one side form a right triangle, with hypotenuse 13 and one leg 12. Half of BD = sqrt(13^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(169 - 144) = sqrt(25) = 5 meters, so BD = 10 meters. Area of the rhombus = (AC × BD)/2 = (24 × 10)/2 = 120 square meters.

method.method_draft: Use the rhombus diagonal formula. From the text, compute each side of the rhombus as 52/4 = 13 meters and use AC = 24 meters. From the image, note that AC is one diagonal of rhombus ABCD and the other diagonal is BD. In a rhombus, diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so half of AC is 12 and half of BD forms a right triangle with hypotenuse 13. Compute half of BD as sqrt(13^2 - 12^2) = 5, so BD = 10. Then area = (AC * BD)/2 = (24 * 10)/2 = 120.

method.method_draft: Split the rhombus into two congruent triangles along diagonal AC. From the text, each rhombus side is 52/4 = 13 meters and AC = 24 meters. From the image, diagonal AC divides the rhombus into triangles ABC and ADC, each with side lengths 13, 13, and 24. Find the area of one isosceles triangle by dropping an altitude to AC: it bisects AC into two 12-meter segments, so the height is sqrt(13^2 - 12^2) = 5. One triangle has area (1/2)(24)(5) = 60, and the rhombus consists of two such triangles, so the total area is 120.
